task_2.title: Prevent pytest.raises() from crashing on HTTPError formatting edge cases
task_2.description: The 8.0.1 update fixes a runtime edge case in exception formatting so that pytest.raises() no longer crashes when handling certain urllib.error.HTTPError exceptions on affected Python versions. Instead of failing during internal stringification, pytest should continue evaluating the raised exception normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.raises() does not crash when formatting exceptions in edge cases where reading exception notes fails, including urllib.error.HTTPError instances affected by Python runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: ExceptionInfo._stringify_exception must allow pytest.raises() to process BaseException instances even when accessing an exception's __notes__ attribute raises KeyError for urllib.error.HTTPError on affected Python 3.11-and-earlier runtimes. In that case, pytest.raises() should continue using the exception string without notes instead of failing inside exception formatting.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest.raises() inspects an exception, internal formatting should be resilient to Python-specific attribute-access quirks. If optional exception notes cannot be read for this HTTPError edge case, pytest should still complete normal exception handling rather than crashing.

constraints.grounded: The safeguard is limited to the observable edge case of KeyError while reading __notes__ from urllib.error.HTTPError on affected Python versions. Normal note handling for other exceptions, and non-covered failures while accessing exception metadata, should not be silently altered.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only suppress the known formatting edge case and preserve existing behavior for normal exception rendering and unrelated errors.

behavior: pytest.raises() no longer fails because exception stringification crashes while processing certain urllib.error.HTTPError exceptions.
If exception notes cannot be obtained for the covered HTTPError edge case, pytest formats the exception using its base string representation and proceeds without notes.
Exception note rendering remains available for exceptions whose optional notes can be accessed normally.
Unexpected note-access failures outside the covered compatibility case continue to surface rather than being broadly swallowed.
acceptance_criteria: When code under pytest.raises() raises urllib.error.HTTPError in the affected Python compatibility scenario, pytest should report and match the expected exception instead of crashing during formatting.
When an exception provides readable notes, pytest should continue including those notes in its formatted exception text.
When the covered HTTPError edge case occurs, the absence of readable notes should not prevent pytest.raises() from completing its normal exception handling flow.
When note access fails for unrelated cases outside the covered compatibility condition, pytest should not silently mask those failures as part of this fix.

task_3.title: Fix pytest.warns handling for custom warning subclasses
task_3.description: Pytest 8.0.1 fixes a regression in pytest.warns() so custom warning subclasses with multi-argument constructors are handled correctly when a match check fails. Instead of triggering an unrelated constructor error while processing the emitted warning, pytest now reports the normal warning-mismatch failure for the original warning object.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.warns() handles custom warning subclasses with more than one constructor parameter without raising unrelated errors when the expected warning message pattern does not match.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.warns() is used with a warning class and a match pattern, and code emits an instance of a custom warning subclass whose __init__ accepts multiple arguments, a non-matching warning message must result in pytest's normal warn-mismatch failure path rather than a TypeError caused by reconstructing the warning. The warning should continue to be processed using its original message object and warning category so observable failure reporting remains consistent with other warning types.
expectation.conceptual: Using pytest.warns() with custom warning types should behave the same as with standard warnings. If the emitted warning is of the expected type but its message does not satisfy the requested match, pytest should report that the expected warning was not matched, not crash with a separate constructor-related error.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve the public behavior of pytest.warns() for ordinary warnings while removing the regression specific to custom warning subclasses with multiple constructor arguments. No new API surface, caller-side workaround, or change to how warnings are emitted by user code should be required.
constraints.conceptual: The patch must be backward-compatible for existing warning assertions and only eliminate the erroneous extra failure mode. Users should not need to rewrite their warning classes or change how they call pytest.warns().

behavior: pytest.warns() must accept emitted instances of custom warning subclasses that carry multiple constructor arguments.
If a match pattern does not match the emitted warning content, the context manager should fail through pytest's standard warning-mismatch outcome instead of raising a constructor-related exception.
Processing unmatched warnings should preserve the original warning object semantics rather than depending on re-instantiating the warning class from derived text.
The warning category associated with the emitted warning should remain the category used for observable warning handling.
acceptance_criteria: When code inside pytest.warns(CustomWarning, match=...) emits a CustomWarning instance whose class requires multiple constructor arguments, execution should not fail with TypeError during warning handling.
When the emitted CustomWarning instance does not satisfy the provided match pattern, pytest.warns(...) should report the normal warn-mismatch failure for the warning assertion.
When the emitted warning matches the expected warning type, support for custom warning subclasses with structured constructor arguments should remain intact.
Existing uses of pytest.warns() with standard warning classes should continue to behave the same after the upgrade.

task_1.title: Handle Python 3.13 username lookup failures in pytest temp directory setup
task_1.description: Pytest 8.0.1 fixes temporary-directory initialization so environments where `getpass.getuser()` now raises `OSError` in Python 3.13 do not crash temp path setup. Instead, pytest treats the username as unavailable and continues with its existing fallback temp-directory behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest temporary directory initialization does not fail when current-user detection cannot be completed in Python 3.13 environments, and that `tmp_path`-related behavior continues with a safe fallback instead of surfacing the username lookup error.

expectation.grounded: When pytest resolves the base temporary directory used by `tmp_path` and `tmp_path_factory`, failures from `getpass.getuser()` that raise `OSError` must be handled the same way as existing unsupported-user lookup failures. Pytest should treat the username as unavailable, avoid propagating that exception, and continue using the fallback temporary-directory naming path.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should remain usable even if the runtime cannot determine the current username during temporary-directory setup. In that case, temp-path features should keep working by falling back to a generic user identity instead of aborting the run.

constraints.grounded: Successful username lookup behavior must remain unchanged. Existing handling for `ImportError` and `KeyError` during username resolution must continue to work. Only the username lookup failure should be suppressed; unrelated filesystem and ownership errors from creating or validating the temporary directory must still surface normally.
constraints.conceptual: This fix must only broaden compatibility for username lookup failures and must not alter normal temp-directory behavior or hide other real setup errors.

behavior: If `getpass.getuser()` raises `OSError` while pytest is determining the session temporary root, pytest no longer propagates that exception.
When username lookup fails with `OSError`, pytest behaves as if no username is available and proceeds with its existing fallback temp-directory identity.
Runs that already succeed because username lookup works, or because lookup fails with previously handled error types, continue to behave the same way.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest starts in an environment where `getpass.getuser()` raises `OSError`, it should still initialize the base temporary directory and continue execution.
When username lookup cannot be completed, `tmp_path` and `tmp_path_factory` should remain usable through pytest's fallback temp-directory behavior.
When `getpass.getuser()` succeeds, pytest should continue to use the resolved username in its normal temporary-directory workflow.
When temporary-directory creation or ownership validation fails for reasons unrelated to username lookup, pytest should still report those errors.

task_4.title: Preserve control-flow outcomes inside pytest.warns()
task_4.description: Pytest 8.0.1 fixes a regression from 8.0.0 where control-flow outcomes raised inside `pytest.warns()` could be masked by the warning checker when no matching warning was emitted. The upgrade restores the original skip, fail, exit, xfail, or interrupt behavior while leaving normal warning assertion semantics in place.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that control-flow outcomes raised inside `pytest.warns()` are not suppressed by the warning checker and continue to determine the observable result even when no matching warning is emitted.

expectation.grounded: `pytest.warns()` should allow control-flow outcomes such as `pytest.skip()`, `pytest.fail()`, `pytest.xfail()`, `pytest.exit()`, and non-`Exception` interruptions to propagate out of the context manager. When one of these outcomes occurs inside the block, `pytest.warns()` must not replace it with its usual missing-warning failure. Existing behavior for successful warning capture and ordinary exceptions should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: A warning assertion block should not convert a skip, expected failure, explicit pytest termination, or interrupt into a warning-related failure. If execution leaves the block because of a control-flow outcome, users should observe that original outcome rather than a false warning assertion failure.

constraints.grounded: Retain the normal contract of `pytest.warns()` when no control-flow outcome occurs: matching warnings still satisfy the context manager, and the missing-warning failure still applies when the expected warning is absent during otherwise normal execution or ordinary exception handling.
constraints.conceptual: Only the regression around control-flow outcomes should change. Standard warning assertion behavior, including failure when an expected warning truly does not occur, must continue to work as before.

behavior: `pytest.warns()` no longer suppresses control-flow outcomes raised inside the context manager when no matching warning is produced.

If `pytest.skip()`, `pytest.fail()`, `pytest.xfail()`, or `pytest.exit()` occurs inside `pytest.warns()`, that original outcome remains the user-visible result instead of being replaced by a missing-warning failure.
Interrupt-style conditions outside normal `Exception` handling also propagate through `pytest.warns()` rather than being converted into a warning assertion failure.
Normal `pytest.warns()` validation for expected warnings and ordinary exceptions is preserved.
acceptance_criteria: When code inside `pytest.warns()` triggers `pytest.skip()` before emitting the expected warning, it should be reported as skipped rather than as a warning assertion failure.

When code inside `pytest.warns()` triggers `pytest.fail()`, `pytest.xfail()`, or `pytest.exit()` before emitting the expected warning, the corresponding pytest outcome should be preserved as the observable result.
When execution inside `pytest.warns()` is interrupted by a non-ordinary exception such as a keyboard interrupt, the interrupt should propagate instead of being replaced by a missing-warning failure.
When code inside `pytest.warns()` completes normally without a matching warning and without a control-flow outcome, it should still fail according to the existing warning assertion contract.
When the expected warning is emitted inside `pytest.warns()`, the context manager should continue to succeed as before.

task_5.title: Restore autouse fixtures for doctest modules
task_5.description: Pytest 8.0.1 restores a behavior that regressed in 8.0.0: doctests collected from a module must once again honor autouse fixtures declared in that same module, so doctest execution sees the expected automatic setup and teardown without changing normal import-error handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that doctests collected from a module continue to honor `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` fixtures defined in that same module, restoring the behavior that regressed in pytest 8.0.0.

expectation.grounded: When pytest runs with `--doctest-modules`, doctests from an imported module should pick up module-defined `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` fixtures through normal fixture discovery so their automatic setup and teardown apply during doctest execution. This restoration must preserve the existing `doctest_ignore_import_errors` behavior for modules that fail to import, and it does not add direct fixture injection into doctest examples.
expectation.conceptual: Doctests should behave like other tests in the same module with respect to automatic fixtures: if a module declares setup that is meant to run automatically, doctest examples in that module should observe it without requiring users to restructure their tests.

constraints.grounded: Do not change doctest support to allow explicit fixture arguments or fixture lookup inside doctest examples; only restore automatic application of autouse fixtures defined on the doctest module. Keep doctest collection/import failure outcomes consistent with the configured import-error policy.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the fix to restoring missing automatic fixture behavior for doctests, without expanding the doctest feature set or changing unrelated collection semantics.

behavior: Doctests collected from a Python module via `--doctest-modules` now discover autouse fixtures declared in that same module before the doctests run.
Automatic fixture side effects and lifecycle behavior become visible to doctest examples in the module again, matching expected pre-8.0.0 behavior.
Modules that cannot be imported still follow the configured doctest import-error handling instead of introducing new failure or skip behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a module collected with `--doctest-modules` declares an autouse fixture and a doctest in that module depends on the fixture's automatic setup, the doctest should execute with that setup in effect.
When the autouse fixture mutates module-visible state during setup, doctest examples in the same module should observe the updated state rather than the pre-fixture state.
When a doctest module fails to import, pytest should continue to skip or raise according to `doctest_ignore_import_errors`.
When running doctests from a module, users should not need to request fixtures explicitly in doctest code for module-level autouse behavior to take effect.

task_6.title: Restore stable collection order for individually selected parametrized tests
task_6.description: Pytest 8.0.1 fixes a regression introduced in 8.0.0 where collecting a specifically selected test could reverse the order of discovered items. The upgrade restores the expected declaration order when users run an individual parametrized test or other targeted node selection, so execution and reporting stay consistent with normal collection.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that targeted pytest collection does not reverse item order. When users run an individually selected parametrized test or another specific node selection, collected items should appear and execute in the same logical order as standard collection rather than in reverse.

expectation.grounded: In pytest 8.0.1, collection through node-id-based selection must preserve the original order of matched items and collectors. For tests expanded by `@pytest.mark.parametrize`, invoking a specific test function such as `path::test_name` should produce parameterized items in the same parameter declaration order as full-file collection, instead of reversing them during `Session` pruning of matched subnodes.
expectation.conceptual: Selecting a subset of tests should not change their order. Users should see the same sequence of parametrized cases and other matched collected items whether they run the whole file or target a specific test node.

constraints.grounded: The fix must be order-preserving only; it must not change which items are matched by node-id selection, and it must not alter the observable collection order for unaffected collection modes beyond removing the unintended reversal introduced in 8.0.0.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should correct the regression without changing what gets collected. It should only restore consistent ordering for targeted runs and avoid introducing new ordering surprises elsewhere.

behavior: When pytest collects a specifically selected test node, matched subnodes are processed in a way that preserves their original collection order instead of reversing it.
For `@pytest.mark.parametrize`, targeting a test function by node id yields parameterized cases in declaration order.
Collection and execution order for targeted selections is aligned with the order users already observe during normal file-level collection.
The change affects runtime-visible collection and reporting order, not the set of collected items.
acceptance_criteria: When a parametrized test is declared with parameters in a specific order and the user runs the whole file, pytest should continue to collect the generated cases in that order.
When the same parametrized test is invoked by selecting the individual test function via node id, pytest should collect and run the generated cases in the same order as the full-file invocation.
When pytest prunes collection to match a targeted node selection, it should preserve the original ordering of matched child nodes rather than returning them in reverse.
When users upgrade from 8.0.0 to 8.0.1, previously reversed ordering during targeted collection should no longer occur.
